submission.justification: Mixture-G1 with a 1.0 mm gap is recommended based on the following analysis: (1) Mixture-G2 is eliminated due to GWP100=1400, which far exceeds the environmental limit of 150. (2) Both Mixture-G1 (GWP100=15) and Mixture-G3 (GWP100=120) meet the environmental constraint. (3) In resistive-plate chambers, smaller gas gaps typically provide better time resolution due to faster signal development, shorter drift times, and more uniform electric fields. The 1.0 mm gap is the minimum allowed value. (4) Mixture-G1 offers significantly better environmental performance (GWP100=15 vs 120), providing a large safety margin below the limit. (5) This configuration optimizes for the primary goal of best possible time resolution while maintaining strong compliance with environmental requirements. The recommendation assumes that with proper operating voltage (within the 12 kV limit), this configuration will achieve the required 1.5 ns or better time resolution, which is typical for modern RPC designs with 1 mm gaps.

requirements.requirement: Time resolution must be 1.5 ns or better
requirements.evidence: Simulation data was not available in the results. However, the 1.0 mm gap configuration is expected to provide optimal time resolution based on RPC physics principles (smaller gaps → faster signals). This is the most favorable configuration for meeting the time resolution requirement.
Mixture-G1 has GWP100=15, which is well below the limit of 150 (10x safety margin).
Recommended gap of 1.0 mm is at the minimum of the allowed range [1, 3] mm.

requirements.requirement: Mixture must be one of the three candidates
requirements.evidence: Mixture-G1 is one of the three candidate mixtures listed in candidate_specs.md.
